{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0168wTgnWjfrQHofqEXhSFba","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/inlines.py has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1426ab3b-27b1-4ec8-bce6-bdc563b1d55e","uuid":"799b3261-fe2d-4f36-93bf-d2af5f2de2b7","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:41:28.579Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/inlines.py","oldString":"def _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the code span HTML for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    width = len(opener.group())\n    content_start = opener.end()\n    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n            return f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", closer.end()\n    return None","newString":"def _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[Html, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the code span node for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    width = len(opener.group())\n    content_start = opener.end()\n    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n            return Html(f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", content), closer.end()\n    return None","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 2: inline parsing.\n\nResponsibility: parse the raw text of paragraphs and headings into inline nodes with the\ndelimiter-stack algorithms (look for link or image, process emphasis), using the reference map\nfrom `mdparser.refs`.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference\nfrom mdparser.links import LinkTail, match_inline_link, match_reference_tail\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url\n\n# Inline nodes. A delimiter run is a `Text` node until emphasis consumes some of its characters;\n# whatever is left over is literal text. Everything else is already-rendered `Html`.\n# The bracket openers `[` and `![` are also `Text` nodes until a link or image closes over them.\nBRACKET_MARKERS = (\"[\", \"![\")\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Text:\n    \"\"\"An unconsumed run of `*` or `_` characters, escaped on output.\"\"\"\n\n    literal: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Html:\n    \"\"\"Rendered inline HTML: text, a code span, an autolink, raw HTML, or a decoded reference.\n\n    `text` is the node's plain-text value, used for image alt text: markup is dropped, and the\n    characters are unescaped.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    html: str\n    text: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Element:\n    \"\"\"An emphasis element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its opener and closer.\"\"\"\n\n    tag: str\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Link:\n    \"\"\"A link element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its brackets, already processed.\"\"\"\n\n    href: str\n    title: str | None\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Image:\n    \"\"\"An image. Its children are the nodes of its description, already processed; they give the alt text.\"\"\"\n\n    destination: str\n    title: str | None\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\nNode = Text | Html | Element | Link | Image\n\n\n@dataclass(eq=False)\nclass Delimiter:\n    \"\"\"A delimiter stack entry. Identity matters, so entries compare by object, not by value.\n\n    `previous` and `next` link the stack from the bottom sentinel upward. `node` is the `Text` node\n    holding the run, or None for the bottom sentinel. A bracket opener is an entry whose `char` is\n    `[` or `![`, and `position` is the source index where that opener starts.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    node: Text | None\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    original_length: int\n    can_open: bool\n    can_close: bool\n    active: bool = True\n    previous: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n    next: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n    position: int = 0\n\n# The body of an autolink: everything between `<` and `>` except ASCII control characters, space,\n# `<` and `>`. The URI and email rules are checked against this body.\nAUTOLINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"<([^\\x00-\\x20\\x7f<>]*)>\")\n# A scheme is 2 to 32 characters: an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`.\nURI_SCHEME_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\\-]{1,31}:\")\n# The non-normative HTML5 email address regex from the spec, without its anchors.\nEMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+\"\n    r\"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\"\n    r\"(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*\"\n)\n\n# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. Code spans open and close on equal-length runs.\nBACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"`+\")\n\n# Whitespace in a raw HTML tag: spaces and tabs, with at most one line ending.\n_WS = r\"[ \\t]*(?:\\n[ \\t]*)?\"\n# Whitespace that must be present: an attribute cannot follow its tag name or value directly.\n_WS_REQUIRED = r\"(?=[ \\t\\n])\" + _WS\n_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\n_ATTR_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n# An unquoted value is nonempty and has no whitespace, quote, `=`, `<`, `>` or backtick.\n_UNQUOTED_VALUE = r\"[^ \\t\\n\\r\\\"'=<>`]+\"\n_ATTR_VALUE = rf\"(?:{_UNQUOTED_VALUE}|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\")\"\n_ATTRIBUTE = rf\"{_WS_REQUIRED}{_ATTR_NAME}(?:{_WS}={_WS}{_ATTR_VALUE})?\"\n# The raw HTML grammars from the spec, tried in order. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.\nRAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(\n    re.compile(pattern)\n    for pattern in (\n        rf\"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>\",\n        rf\"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>\",\n        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.\n        r\"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)\",\n        r\"<\\?(?s:.*?)\\?>\",\n        r\"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>\",\n        r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[(?s:.*?)\\]\\]>\",\n    )\n)\n\n\ndef parse_inline(raw: str, references: ReferenceMap | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Inline parser hook: return the HTML for a block's raw content.\n\n    The scan runs left to right. At each special character the constructs that start there are\n    tried, and the first one that matches is taken whole. Code spans, autolinks and raw HTML have\n    equal precedence, so whichever starts first wins. A backtick string with no closing run of the\n    same length is literal text, and the whole run is consumed. An autolink or raw HTML tag is taken\n    whole, so a backslash inside it stays literal. A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that\n    character, so `\\\\<` and `\\\\`` do not open a construct. A recognized character reference is\n    decoded and its character is escaped text, so `&#42;` never opens structure. A run of `*` or `_`\n    becomes a delimiter run: a text node pushed on the delimiter stack, which process_emphasis then\n    pairs into emphasis. A `[` or `![` pushes a bracket opener on the same stack, and a `]` runs the\n    look-for-link-or-image procedure against the nearest opener, using `references` for reference\n    forms. Everything else is escaped text.\n    \"\"\"\n    references = ReferenceMap() if references is None else references\n    nodes: list[Node] = []\n    stack = DelimiterStack(nodes)\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(raw):\n        char = raw[index]\n        if char == \"`\":\n            code_span = _match_code_span(raw, index)\n            if code_span is not None:\n                node, index = code_span\n                nodes.append(node)\n                continue\n            run_end = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, index).end()\n            nodes.append(_text(raw[index:run_end]))\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        if char == \"<\":\n            autolink = _match_autolink(raw, index)\n            if autolink is not None:\n                node, index = autolink\n                nodes.append(node)\n                continue\n            raw_html_end = _match_raw_html(raw, index)\n            if raw_html_end is not None:\n                nodes.append(_raw(raw[index:raw_html_end]))\n                index = raw_html_end\n                continue\n        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            nodes.append(_text(raw[index + 1]))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char in \"*_\":\n            run_end = _delimiter_run_end(raw, index)\n            _push_delimiter_run(stack, raw, index, run_end)\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        elif char == \"&\":\n            reference = match_reference(raw, index)\n            if reference is not None:\n                # A decoded character is text, so it is escaped like any other text.\n                value, index = reference\n                nodes.append(_text(value))\n                continue\n        elif char == \"[\":\n            _push_bracket(stack, \"[\", index)\n            index += 1\n            continue\n        elif char == \"!\" and raw[index + 1 : index + 2] == \"[\":\n            _push_bracket(stack, \"![\", index)\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char == \"]\":\n            index = _close_bracket(stack, raw, index, references)\n            continue\n        nodes.append(_text(char))\n        index += 1\n    stack.process_emphasis()\n    return render_nodes(nodes)\n\n\ndef _text(value: str) -> Html:\n    \"\"\"A literal run of text: escaped in the output, and its own plain text.\"\"\"\n    return Html(escape_html(value), value)\n\n\ndef _raw(value: str) -> Html:\n    \"\"\"Raw HTML, output as written. Its plain text is the same source, escaped only when used as alt.\"\"\"\n    return Html(value, value)\n\n\ndef render_nodes(nodes: list[Node]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a node list to HTML. Leftover delimiter runs and brackets are escaped literal text.\"\"\"\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    for node in nodes:\n        if isinstance(node, Html):\n            parts.append(node.html)\n        elif isinstance(node, Text):\n            parts.append(escape_html(node.literal))\n        elif isinstance(node, Link):\n            parts.append(_render_link(node))\n        elif isinstance(node, Image):\n            parts.append(_render_image(node))\n        else:\n            parts.append(f\"<{node.tag}>{render_nodes(node.children)}</{node.tag}>\")\n    return \"\".join(parts)\n\n\ndef _render_link(link: Link) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link element. The href is percent-encoded then escaped; an empty title is omitted.\"\"\"\n    href = escape_html(percent_encode_url(link.href))\n    title = f' title=\"{escape_html(link.title)}\"' if link.title else \"\"\n    return f'<a href=\"{href}\"{title}>{render_nodes(link.children)}</a>'\n\n\ndef _render_image(image: Image) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render an image. The src is percent-encoded then escaped; alt is the escaped plain text of the description.\"\"\"\n    src = escape_html(percent_encode_url(image.destination))\n    alt = escape_html(_plain_text(image.children))\n    title = f' title=\"{escape_html(image.title)}\"' if image.title else \"\"\n    return f'<img src=\"{src}\" alt=\"{alt}\"{title} />'\n\n\ndef _plain_text(nodes: list[Node]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The plain text of a node list: emphasis, links and images keep their text, and markup is dropped.\"\"\"\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    for node in nodes:\n        if isinstance(node, Html):\n            parts.append(node.text)\n        elif isinstance(node, Text):\n            parts.append(node.literal)\n        else:\n            parts.append(_plain_text(node.children))\n    return \"\".join(parts)\n\n\ndef _push_bracket(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", marker: str, start: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Push a bracket opener for `[` or `![`, which starts at `start`, as literal text until closed.\"\"\"\n    stack.push(Text(marker), marker, len(marker), True, False)\n    stack.top.position = start\n\n\ndef _close_bracket(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", raw: str, close: int, references: ReferenceMap) -> int:\n    \"\"\"The look-for-link-or-image procedure at the `]` at `close`. Return the index to resume at.\n\n    The nearest opener is used. With no opener, or an inactive one, the `]` is literal. Otherwise the\n    inline form, then the reference forms, are tried after the `]`. A match becomes a link, or an\n    image construct, over the nodes after the opener. A failed match removes the opener and leaves\n    the `]` literal. A link also deactivates every earlier `[` opener, so links never nest.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = stack.nearest_bracket()\n    if opener is None or not opener.active:\n        if opener is not None:\n            stack.remove_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(_text(\"]\"))\n        return close + 1\n    text = raw[opener.position + len(opener.char) : close]\n    tail: LinkTail | None = match_inline_link(raw, close + 1)\n    if tail is None:\n        tail = match_reference_tail(raw, close + 1, text, references)\n    if tail is None:\n        stack.remove_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(_text(\"]\"))\n        return close + 1\n    if opener.char == \"![\":\n        children = stack.close_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(Image(tail.destination, tail.title, children))\n    else:\n        stack.deactivate_bracket_openers(opener)\n        children = stack.close_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(Link(tail.destination, tail.title, children))\n    return tail.end\n\n\ndef _delimiter_run_end(raw: str, start: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the maximal run of the delimiter character at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start + 1\n    while end < len(raw) and raw[end] == raw[start]:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _push_delimiter_run(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", raw: str, start: int, end: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append the run raw[start:end] as a text node and push its stack entry with flanking flags.\n\n    The characters before and after the run decide flanking. The start and end of the line count\n    as whitespace, so a missing neighbour is passed as None.\n    \"\"\"\n    char = raw[start]\n    before = raw[start - 1] if start > 0 else None\n    after = raw[end] if end < len(raw) else None\n    left_flanking, right_flanking = _flanking(before, after)\n    if char == \"*\":\n        can_open, can_close = left_flanking, right_flanking\n    else:\n        can_open = left_flanking and (not right_flanking or _is_punctuation(before))\n        can_close = right_flanking and (not left_flanking or _is_punctuation(after))\n    stack.push(Text(char * (end - start)), char, end - start, can_open, can_close)\n\n\ndef _is_whitespace(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode whitespace: tab, line feed, form feed, carriage return, or a Zs character.\n\n    The start and end of the line are passed as None and count as whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    return char is None or char in \"\\t\\n\\f\\r\" or unicodedata.category(char) == \"Zs\"\n\n\ndef _is_punctuation(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode punctuation or symbol: categories P* and S*. None (the line edge) is not one.\"\"\"\n    return char is not None and unicodedata.category(char)[0] in \"PS\"\n\n\ndef _flanking(before: str | None, after: str | None) -> tuple[bool, bool]:\n    \"\"\"Return (left-flanking, right-flanking) for a delimiter run with these neighbours.\"\"\"\n    left_flanking = not _is_whitespace(after) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(after) or _is_whitespace(before) or _is_punctuation(before)\n    )\n    right_flanking = not _is_whitespace(before) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(before) or _is_whitespace(after) or _is_punctuation(after)\n    )\n    return left_flanking, right_flanking\n\n\nclass DelimiterStack:\n    \"\"\"The delimiter stack: a doubly linked list of `Delimiter` entries over a sibling node list.\n\n    The bottom sentinel is never removed, so `stack_bottom` is always an entry. `process_emphasis`\n    wraps the nodes between a matched pair inside `nodes`, so every delimiter it touches must be a\n    sibling of the others in that list.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, nodes: list[Node]) -> None:\n        self.nodes = nodes\n        self.bottom = Delimiter(None, \"\", 0, 0, False, False)\n        self.top = self.bottom\n\n    def push(self, node: Text, char: str, length: int, can_open: bool, can_close: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append a delimiter entry for a run that is already a `Text` node in `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self.nodes.append(node)\n        entry = Delimiter(node, char, length, length, can_open, can_close, previous=self.top)\n        self.top.next = entry\n        self.top = entry\n\n    def process_emphasis(self, stack_bottom: Delimiter | None = None) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Pair delimiter runs above `stack_bottom` into em and strong (Appendix algorithm).\n\n        `openers_bottom` is keyed by delimiter character, the closer's original length mod 3, and\n        whether the closer can also open. Each key holds the lowest entry an opener search may\n        reach, so a failed search is not repeated. Unmatched runs stay as literal text.\n        \"\"\"\n        bottom = self.bottom if stack_bottom is None else stack_bottom\n        openers_bottom: dict[tuple[str, int, bool], Delimiter] = {}\n        closer = self._first_closer(bottom.next)\n        while closer is not None:\n            key = (closer.char, closer.original_length % 3, closer.can_open)\n            opener = self._find_opener(closer, bottom, openers_bottom.get(key, bottom))\n            if opener is None:\n                openers_bottom[key] = closer.previous\n                following = closer.next\n                if not closer.can_open:\n                    self._unlink(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n                continue\n            strong = opener.length >= 2 and closer.length >= 2\n            used = 2 if strong else 1\n            opener.length -= used\n            closer.length -= used\n            self._unlink_between(opener, closer)\n            self._sync_literal(opener)\n            self._sync_literal(closer)\n            self._wrap(opener.node, closer.node, \"strong\" if strong else \"em\")\n            if opener.length == 0:\n                self._drop(opener)\n            if closer.length == 0:\n                following = closer.next\n                self._drop(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n        bottom.next = None\n        self.top = bottom\n\n    def nearest_bracket(self) -> Delimiter | None:\n        \"\"\"The bracket opener nearest the top of the stack, or None when there is none.\"\"\"\n        entry = self.top\n        while entry is not None and entry.char not in BRACKET_MARKERS:\n            entry = entry.previous\n        return entry\n\n    def remove_bracket(self, opener: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove a bracket opener from the stack. Its `[` or `![` text stays as literal text.\"\"\"\n        self._unlink(opener)\n\n    def deactivate_bracket_openers(self, opener: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Mark every `[` opener below `opener` inactive, so a link cannot form around a link.\"\"\"\n        entry = opener.previous\n        while entry is not None:\n            if entry.char == \"[\":\n                entry.active = False\n            entry = entry.previous\n\n    def close_bracket(self, opener: Delimiter) -> list[Node]:\n        \"\"\"Process emphasis inside a matched bracket and take its content out of the node list.\n\n        Every delimiter above the opener leaves the stack, and the opener's own text node is removed.\n        Return the nodes that sat after the opener, in order, as the content of the new element.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.process_emphasis(stack_bottom=opener)\n        start = self._index_of(opener.node)\n        content = self.nodes[start + 1 :]\n        del self.nodes[start:]\n        self._unlink(opener)\n        return content\n\n    def _first_closer(self, entry: Delimiter | None) -> Delimiter | None:\n        while entry is not None and not entry.can_close:\n            entry = entry.next\n        return entry\n\n    def _find_opener(\n        self, closer: Delimiter, bottom: Delimiter, openers_bottom: Delimiter\n    ) -> Delimiter | None:\n        \"\"\"Search back from the closer for a matching opener above both lower bounds, or None.\n\n        Under the multiple-of-3 rule a pair is skipped when one run can both open and close and the\n        original lengths sum to a multiple of 3, unless both lengths are multiples of 3.\n        \"\"\"\n        potential = closer.previous\n        while potential is not None and potential is not bottom and potential is not openers_bottom:\n            odd_match = (\n                (closer.can_open or potential.can_close)\n                and closer.original_length % 3 != 0\n                and (potential.original_length + closer.original_length) % 3 == 0\n            )\n            if potential.char == closer.char and potential.can_open and not odd_match:\n                return potential\n            potential = potential.previous\n        return None\n\n    def _unlink(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an entry from the stack. Its node stays in `nodes` as text.\"\"\"\n        entry.previous.next = entry.next\n        if entry.next is not None:\n            entry.next.previous = entry.previous\n        else:\n            self.top = entry.previous\n\n    def _unlink_between(self, opener: Delimiter, closer: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove every entry strictly between an opener and a closer from the stack.\"\"\"\n        opener.next = closer\n        closer.previous = opener\n\n    def _drop(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an exhausted run from the stack and from `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self._unlink(entry)\n        del self.nodes[self._index_of(entry.node)]\n\n    def _sync_literal(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        entry.node.literal = entry.char * entry.length\n\n    def _wrap(self, opener_node: Text, closer_node: Text, tag: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the nodes between opener and closer into a new element after the opener.\"\"\"\n        start = self._index_of(opener_node) + 1\n        end = self._index_of(closer_node)\n        self.nodes[start:end] = [Element(tag, self.nodes[start:end])]\n\n    def _index_of(self, node: Node) -> int:\n        for index, candidate in enumerate(self.nodes):\n            if candidate is node:\n                return index\n        raise ValueError(\"delimiter node is not in the node list\")\n\n\ndef _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the code span HTML for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    width = len(opener.group())\n    content_start = opener.end()\n    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n            return f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", closer.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _normalize_code_content(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Turn line endings into spaces, then strip one space from each end when both ends are spaces.\n\n    Stripping is skipped when the content is entirely spaces. Only U+0020 counts as a space.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")\n    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == \" \" and text[-1] == \" \" and text.strip(\" \"):\n        return text[1:-1]\n    return text\n\n\ndef _match_autolink(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the link HTML for an autolink at `start` and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    match = AUTOLINK_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    if match is None:\n        return None\n    body = match.group(1)\n    if URI_SCHEME_PATTERN.match(body):\n        href = body\n    elif EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(body):\n        href = \"mailto:\" + body\n    else:\n        return None\n    return _link_html(href, body), match.end()\n\n\ndef _match_raw_html(raw: str, start: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the raw HTML construct at `start`, or None if none matches.\"\"\"\n    for pattern in RAW_HTML_PATTERNS:\n        match = pattern.match(raw, start)\n        if match is not None:\n            return match.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _link_html(href: str, text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link: the href is percent-encoded then escaped; the label is escaped text.\"\"\"\n    return f'<a href=\"{escape_html(percent_encode_url(href))}\">{escape_html(text)}</a>'\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":494,"oldLines":8,"newStart":494,"newLines":8,"lines":["         raise ValueError(\"delimiter node is not in the node list\")"," "," ","-def _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:","-    \"\"\"Return the code span HTML for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.","+def _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[Html, int] | None:","+    \"\"\"Return the code span node for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it."," ","     The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no","     such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text."]},{"oldStart":506,"oldLines":7,"newStart":506,"newLines":7,"lines":["     for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):","         if len(closer.group()) == width:","             content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])","-            return f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", closer.end()","+            return Html(f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", content), closer.end()","     return None"," "," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_0168wTgnWjfrQHofqEXhSFba","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

Everything else is already-rendered `Html`.\n# The bracket openers `[` and `![` are also `Text` nodes until a link or image closes over them.\nBRACKET_MARKERS = (\"[\", \"![\")\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Text:\n    \"\"\"An unconsumed run of `*` or `_` characters, escaped on output.\"\"\"\n\n    literal: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Html:\n    \"\"\"Rendered inline HTML: text, a code span, an autolink, raw HTML, or a decoded reference.\n\n    `text` is the node's plain-text value, used for image alt text: markup is dropped, and the\n    characters are unescaped.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    html: str\n    text: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Element:\n    \"\"\"An emphasis element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its opener and closer.\"\"\"\n\n    tag: str\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Link:\n    \"\"\"A link element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its brackets, already processed.\"\"\"\n\n    href: str\n    title: str | None\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Image:\n    \"\"\"An image. Its children are the nodes of its description, already processed; they give the alt text.\"\"\"\n\n    destination: str\n    title: str | None\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\nNode = Text | Html | Element | Link | Image\n\n\n@dataclass(eq=False)\nclass Delimiter:\n    \"\"\"A delimiter stack entry. Identity matters, so entries compare by object, not by value.\n\n    `previous` and `next` link the stack from the bottom sentinel upward. `node` is the `Text` node\n    holding the run, or None for the bottom sentinel. A bracket opener is an entry whose `char` is\n    `[` or `![`, and `position` is the source index where that opener starts.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    node: Text | None\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    original_length: int\n    can_open: bool\n    can_close: bool\n    active: bool = True\n    previous: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n    next: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n    position: int = 0\n\n# The body of an autolink: everything between `<` and `>` except ASCII control characters, space,\n# `<` and `>`. The URI and email rules are checked against this body.\nAUTOLINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"<([^\\x00-\\x20\\x7f<>]*)>\")\n# A scheme is 2 to 32 characters: an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`.\nURI_SCHEME_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\\-]{1,31}:\")\n# The non-normative HTML5 email address regex from the spec, without its anchors.\nEMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+\"\n    r\"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\"\n    r\"(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*\"\n)\n\n# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. Code spans open and close on equal-length runs.\nBACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"`+\")\n\n# Whitespace in a raw HTML tag: spaces and tabs, with at most one line ending.\n_WS = r\"[ \\t]*(?:\\n[ \\t]*)?\"\n# Whitespace that must be present: an attribute cannot follow its tag name or value directly.\n_WS_REQUIRED = r\"(?=[ \\t\\n])\" + _WS\n_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\n_ATTR_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n# An unquoted value is nonempty and has no whitespace, quote, `=`, `<`, `>` or backtick.\n_UNQUOTED_VALUE = r\"[^ \\t\\n\\r\\\"'=<>`]+\"\n_ATTR_VALUE = rf\"(?:{_UNQUOTED_VALUE}|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\")\"\n_ATTRIBUTE = rf\"{_WS_REQUIRED}{_ATTR_NAME}(?:{_WS}={_WS}{_ATTR_VALUE})?\"\n# The raw HTML grammars from the spec, tried in order. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.\nRAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(\n    re.compile(pattern)\n    for pattern in (\n        rf\"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>\",\n        rf\"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>\",\n        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.\n        r\"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)\",\n        r\"<\\?(?s:.*?)\\?>\",\n        r\"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>\",\n        r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[(?s:.*?)\\]\\]>\",\n    )\n)\n\n\ndef parse_inline(raw: str, references: ReferenceMap | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Inline parser hook: return the HTML for a block's raw content.\n\n    The scan runs left to right. At each special character the constructs that start there are\n    tried, and the first one that matches is taken whole. Code spans, autolinks and raw HTML have\n    equal precedence, so whichever starts first wins. A backtick string with no closing run of the\n    same length is literal text, and the whole run is consumed. An autolink or raw HTML tag is taken\n    whole, so a backslash inside it stays literal. A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that\n    character, so `\\\\<` and `\\\\`` do not open a construct. A recognized character reference is\n    decoded and its character is escaped text, so `&#42;` never opens structure. A run of `*` or `_`\n    becomes a delimiter run: a text node pushed on the delimiter stack, which process_emphasis then\n    pairs into emphasis. A `[` or `![` pushes a bracket opener on the same stack, and a `]` runs the\n    look-for-link-or-image procedure against the nearest opener, using `references` for reference\n    forms. Everything else is escaped text.\n    \"\"\"\n    references = ReferenceMap() if references is None else references\n    nodes: list[Node] = []\n    stack = DelimiterStack(nodes)\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(raw):\n        char = raw[index]\n        if char == \"`\":\n            code_span = _match_code_span(raw, index)\n            if code_span is not None:\n                node, index = code_span\n                nodes.append(node)\n                continue\n            run_end = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, index).end()\n            nodes.append(_text(raw[index:run_end]))\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        if char == \"<\":\n            autolink = _match_autolink(raw, index)\n            if autolink is not None:\n                node, index = autolink\n                nodes.append(node)\n                continue\n            raw_html_end = _match_raw_html(raw, index)\n            if raw_html_end is not None:\n                nodes.append(_raw(raw[index:raw_html_end]))\n                index = raw_html_end\n                continue\n        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            nodes.append(_text(raw[index + 1]))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char in \"*_\":\n            run_end = _delimiter_run_end(raw, index)\n            _push_delimiter_run(stack, raw, index, run_end)\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        elif char == \"&\":\n            reference = match_reference(raw, index)\n            if reference is not None:\n                # A decoded character is text, so it is escaped like any other text.\n                value, index = reference\n                nodes.append(_text(value))\n                continue\n        elif char == \"[\":\n            _push_bracket(stack, \"[\", index)\n            index += 1\n            continue\n        elif char == \"!\" and raw[index + 1 : index + 2] == \"[\":\n            _push_bracket(stack, \"![\", index)\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char == \"]\":\n            index = _close_bracket(stack, raw, index, references)\n            continue\n        nodes.append(_text(char))\n        index += 1\n    stack.process_emphasis()\n    return render_nodes(nodes)\n\n\ndef _text(value: str) -> Html:\n    \"\"\"A literal run of text: escaped in the output, and its own plain text.\"\"\"\n    return Html(escape_html(value), value)\n\n\ndef _raw(value: str) -> Html:\n    \"\"\"Raw HTML, output as written. Its plain text is the same source, escaped only when used as alt.\"\"\"\n    return Html(value, value)\n\n\ndef render_nodes(nodes: list[Node]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a node list to HTML. Leftover delimiter runs and brackets are escaped literal text.\"\"\"\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    for node in nodes:\n        if isinstance(node, Html):\n            parts.append(node.html)\n        elif isinstance(node, Text):\n            parts.append(escape_html(node.literal))\n        elif isinstance(node, Link):\n            parts.append(_render_link(node))\n        elif isinstance(node, Image):\n            parts.append(_render_image(node))\n        else:\n            parts.append(f\"<{node.tag}>{render_nodes(node.children)}</{node.tag}>\")\n    return \"\".join(parts)\n\n\ndef _render_link(link: Link) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link element. The href is percent-encoded then escaped; an empty title is omitted.\"\"\"\n    href = escape_html(percent_encode_url(link.href))\n    title = f' title=\"{escape_html(link.title)}\"' if link.title else \"\"\n    return f'<a href=\"{href}\"{title}>{render_nodes(link.children)}</a>'\n\n\ndef _render_image(image: Image) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render an image. The src is percent-encoded then escaped; alt is the escaped plain text of the description.\"\"\"\n    src = escape_html(percent_encode_url(image.destination))\n    alt = escape_html(_plain_text(image.children))\n    title = f' title=\"{escape_html(image.title)}\"' if image.title else \"\"\n    return f'<img src=\"{src}\" alt=\"{alt}\"{title} />'\n\n\ndef _plain_text(nodes: list[Node]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The plain text of a node list: emphasis, links and images keep their text, and markup is dropped.\"\"\"\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    for node in nodes:\n        if isinstance(node, Html):\n            parts.append(node.text)\n        elif isinstance(node, Text):\n            parts.append(node.literal)\n        else:\n            parts.append(_plain_text(node.children))\n    return \"\".join(parts)\n\n\ndef _push_bracket(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", marker: str, start: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Push a bracket opener for `[` or `![`, which starts at `start`, as literal text until closed.\"\"\"\n    stack.push(Text(marker), marker, len(marker), True, False)\n    stack.top.position = start\n\n\ndef _close_bracket(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", raw: str, close: int, references: ReferenceMap) -> int:\n    \"\"\"The look-for-link-or-image procedure at the `]` at `close`. Return the index to resume at.\n\n    The nearest opener is used. With no opener, or an inactive one, the `]` is literal. Otherwise the\n    inline form, then the reference forms, are tried after the `]`. A match becomes a link, or an\n    image construct, over the nodes after the opener. A failed match removes the opener and leaves\n    the `]` literal. A link also deactivates every earlier `[` opener, so links never nest.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = stack.nearest_bracket()\n    if opener is None or not opener.active:\n        if opener is not None:\n            stack.remove_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(_text(\"]\"))\n        return close + 1\n    text = raw[opener.position + len(opener.char) : close]\n    tail: LinkTail | None = match_inline_link(raw, close + 1)\n    if tail is None:\n        tail = match_reference_tail(raw, close + 1, text, references)\n    if tail is None:\n        stack.remove_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(_text(\"]\"))\n        return close + 1\n    if opener.char == \"![\":\n        children = stack.close_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(Image(tail.destination, tail.title, children))\n    else:\n        stack.deactivate_bracket_openers(opener)\n        children = stack.close_bracket(opener)\n        stack.nodes.append(Link(tail.destination, tail.title, children))\n    return tail.end\n\n\ndef _delimiter_run_end(raw: str, start: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the maximal run of the delimiter character at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start + 1\n    while end < len(raw) and raw[end] == raw[start]:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _push_delimiter_run(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", raw: str, start: int, end: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append the run raw[start:end] as a text node and push its stack entry with flanking flags.\n\n    The characters before and after the run decide flanking. The start and end of the line count\n    as whitespace, so a missing neighbour is passed as None.\n    \"\"\"\n    char = raw[start]\n    before = raw[start - 1] if start > 0 else None\n    after = raw[end] if end < len(raw) else None\n    left_flanking, right_flanking = _flanking(before, after)\n    if char == \"*\":\n        can_open, can_close = left_flanking, right_flanking\n    else:\n        can_open = left_flanking and (not right_flanking or _is_punctuation(before))\n        can_close = right_flanking and (not left_flanking or _is_punctuation(after))\n    stack.push(Text(char * (end - start)), char, end - start, can_open, can_close)\n\n\ndef _is_whitespace(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode whitespace: tab, line feed, form feed, carriage return, or a Zs character.\n\n    The start and end of the line are passed as None and count as whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    return char is None or char in \"\\t\\n\\f\\r\" or unicodedata.category(char) == \"Zs\"\n\n\ndef _is_punctuation(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode punctuation or symbol: categories P* and S*. None (the line edge) is not one.\"\"\"\n    return char is not None and unicodedata.category(char)[0] in \"PS\"\n\n\ndef _flanking(before: str | None, after: str | None) -> tuple[bool, bool]:\n    \"\"\"Return (left-flanking, right-flanking) for a delimiter run with these neighbours.\"\"\"\n    left_flanking = not _is_whitespace(after) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(after) or _is_whitespace(before) or _is_punctuation(before)\n    )\n    right_flanking = not _is_whitespace(before) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(before) or _is_whitespace(after) or _is_punctuation(after)\n    )\n    return left_flanking, right_flanking\n\n\nclass DelimiterStack:\n    \"\"\"The delimiter stack: a doubly linked list of `Delimiter` entries over a sibling node list.\n\n    The bottom sentinel is never removed, so `stack_bottom` is always an entry. `process_emphasis`\n    wraps the nodes between a matched pair inside `nodes`, so every delimiter it touches must be a\n    sibling of the others in that list.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, nodes: list[Node]) -> None:\n        self.nodes = nodes\n        self.bottom = Delimiter(None, \"\", 0, 0, False, False)\n        self.top = self.bottom\n\n    def push(self, node: Text, char: str, length: int, can_open: bool, can_close: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append a delimiter entry for a run that is already a `Text` node in `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self.nodes.append(node)\n        entry = Delimiter(node, char, length, length, can_open, can_close, previous=self.top)\n        self.top.next = entry\n        self.top = entry\n\n    def process_emphasis(self, stack_bottom: Delimiter | None = None) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Pair delimiter runs above `stack_bottom` into em and strong (Appendix algorithm).\n\n        `openers_bottom` is keyed by delimiter character, the closer's original length mod 3, and\n        whether the closer can also open. Each key holds the lowest entry an opener search may\n        reach, so a failed search is not repeated. Unmatched runs stay as literal text.\n        \"\"\"\n        bottom = self.bottom if stack_bottom is None else stack_bottom\n        openers_bottom: dict[tuple[str, int, bool], Delimiter] = {}\n        closer = self._first_closer(bottom.next)\n        while closer is not None:\n            key = (closer.char, closer.original_length % 3, closer.can_open)\n            opener = self._find_opener(closer, bottom, openers_bottom.get(key, bottom))\n            if opener is None:\n                openers_bottom[key] = closer.previous\n                following = closer.next\n                if not closer.can_open:\n                    self._unlink(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n                continue\n            strong = opener.length >= 2 and closer.length >= 2\n            used = 2 if strong else 1\n            opener.length -= used\n            closer.length -= used\n            self._unlink_between(opener, closer)\n            self._sync_literal(opener)\n            self._sync_literal(closer)\n            self._wrap(opener.node, closer.node, \"strong\" if strong else \"em\")\n            if opener.length == 0:\n                self._drop(opener)\n            if closer.length == 0:\n                following = closer.next\n                self._drop(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n        bottom.next = None\n        self.top = bottom\n\n    def nearest_bracket(self) -> Delimiter | None:\n        \"\"\"The bracket opener nearest the top of the stack, or None when there is none.\"\"\"\n        entry = self.top\n        while entry is not None and entry.char not in BRACKET_MARKERS:\n            entry = entry.previous\n        return entry\n\n    def remove_bracket(self, opener: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove a bracket opener from the stack. Its `[` or `![` text stays as literal text.\"\"\"\n        self._unlink(opener)\n\n    def deactivate_bracket_openers(self, opener: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Mark every `[` opener below `opener` inactive, so a link cannot form around a link.\"\"\"\n        entry = opener.previous\n        while entry is not None:\n            if entry.char == \"[\":\n                entry.active = False\n            entry = entry.previous\n\n    def close_bracket(self, opener: Delimiter) -> list[Node]:\n        \"\"\"Process emphasis inside a matched bracket and take its content out of the node list.\n\n        Every delimiter above the opener leaves the stack, and the opener's own text node is removed.\n        Return the nodes that sat after the opener, in order, as the content of the new element.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.process_emphasis(stack_bottom=opener)\n        start = self._index_of(opener.node)\n        content = self.nodes[start + 1 :]\n        del self.nodes[start:]\n        self._unlink(opener)\n        return content\n\n    def _first_closer(self, entry: Delimiter | None) -> Delimiter | None:\n        while entry is not None and not entry.can_close:\n            entry = entry.next\n        return entry\n\n    def _find_opener(\n        self, closer: Delimiter, bottom: Delimiter, openers_bottom: Delimiter\n    ) -> Delimiter | None:\n        \"\"\"Search back from the closer for a matching opener above both lower bounds, or None.\n\n        Under the multiple-of-3 rule a pair is skipped when one run can both open and close and the\n        original lengths sum to a multiple of 3, unless both lengths are multiples of 3.\n        \"\"\"\n        potential = closer.previous\n        while potential is not None and potential is not bottom and potential is not openers_bottom:\n            odd_match = (\n                (closer.can_open or potential.can_close)\n                and closer.original_length % 3 != 0\n                and (potential.original_length + closer.original_length) % 3 == 0\n            )\n            if potential.char == closer.char and potential.can_open and not odd_match:\n                return potential\n            potential = potential.previous\n        return None\n\n    def _unlink(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an entry from the stack. Its node stays in `nodes` as text.\"\"\"\n        entry.previous.next = entry.next\n        if entry.next is not None:\n            entry.next.previous = entry.previous\n        else:\n            self.top = entry.previous\n\n    def _unlink_between(self, opener: Delimiter, closer: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove every entry strictly between an opener and a closer from the stack.\"\"\"\n        opener.next = closer\n        closer.previous = opener\n\n    def _drop(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an exhausted run from the stack and from `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self._unlink(entry)\n        del self.nodes[self._index_of(entry.node)]\n\n    def _sync_literal(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        entry.node.literal = entry.char * entry.length\n\n    def _wrap(self, opener_node: Text, closer_node: Text, tag: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the nodes between opener and closer into a new element after the opener.\"\"\"\n        start = self._index_of(opener_node) + 1\n        end = self._index_of(closer_node)\n        self.nodes[start:end] = [Element(tag, self.nodes[start:end])]\n\n    def _index_of(self, node: Node) -> int:\n        for index, candidate in enumerate(self.nodes):\n            if candidate is node:\n                return index\n        raise ValueError(\"delimiter node is not in the node list\")\n\n\ndef _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[Html, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the code span node for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    width = len(opener.group())\n    content_start = opener.end()\n    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n            return Html(f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", content), closer.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _normalize_code_content(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Turn line endings into spaces, then strip one space from each end when both ends are spaces.\n\n    Stripping is skipped when the content is entirely spaces. Only U+0020 counts as a space.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")\n    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == \" \" and text[-1] == \" \" and text.strip(\" \"):\n        return text[1:-1]\n    return text\n\n\ndef _match_autolink(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the link HTML for an autolink at `start` and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    match = AUTOLINK_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    if match is None:\n        return None\n    body = match.group(1)\n    if URI_SCHEME_PATTERN.match(body):\n        href = body\n    elif EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(body):\n        href = \"mailto:\" + body\n    else:\n        return None\n    return _link_html(href, body), match.end()\n\n\ndef _match_raw_html(raw: str, start: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the raw HTML construct at `start`, or None if none matches.\"\"\"\n    for pattern in RAW_HTML_PATTERNS:\n        match = pattern.match(raw, start)\n        if match is not None:\n            return match.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _link_html(href: str, text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link: the href is percent-encoded then escaped; The remaining tests compare the returned HTML string, or the executable's stdout, with its\nexact expected value. Reference maps are built per test, so no state is shared between tests.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom mdparser import inlines\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap\n\n\ndef run_executable(project_root: Path, data: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=data.encode(\"utf-8\"),\n        capture_output=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef references_with(*definitions: tuple[str, str, str | None]) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"A fresh reference map holding each (label, destination, title) definition.\"\"\"\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    for label, destination, title in definitions:\n        references.add(label, destination, title)\n    return references\n\n\ndef parse(source: str, references: ReferenceMap | None = None) -> str:\n    return inlines.parse_inline(source, references)\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Links.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_links_inline_destination_and_title(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC links-inline-destination-and-title: an inline link renders one a element with its parts.\"\"\"\n    text = \"label\"\n    dest = \"/uri\"\n    title = \"the title\"\n    source = \"[\" + text + \"](\" + dest + ' \"' + title + '\")\\n'\n    result = subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<a \") == 1\n    assert ('href=\"' + dest + '\"') in result.stdout\n    assert ('title=\"' + title + '\"') in result.stdout\n    assert (\">\" + text + \"</a>\") in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_links_reference_forms(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC links-reference-forms: full, collapsed and shortcut references each render one a element.\"\"\"\n    definition = \"\\n\\n[foo]: /url\\n\"\n    for use in (\"[text][foo]\", \"[foo][]\", \"[foo]\"):\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n            input=(use + definition).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n            capture_output=True,\n            cwd=project_root,\n            check=False,\n        )\n        print(result.stdout)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<a \") == 1\n\n\ndef test_links_reference_case_insensitive(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC links-reference-case-insensitive: label matching ignores case.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"[FOO]\\n\\n[foo]: /url\\n\")\n    stdout = result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    print(stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert stdout.count(\"<a \") == 1\n\n\ndef test_links_undefined_reference_literal(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC links-undefined-reference-literal: a shortcut reference with no definition stays literal.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"[nothing defined]\\n\")\n    stdout = result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    print(stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert stdout.count(\"<a \") == 0\n\n\ndef test_links_no_nested_links(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC links-no-nested-links: a link inside link text wins and the outer brackets stay literal.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"[foo [bar](/uri)](/uri)\\n\")\n    stdout = result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    print(stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert stdout.count(\"<a \") == 1\n\n\ndef test_links_space_before_parenthesis(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC links-space-before-parenthesis: whitespace between link text and the parenthesis is no link.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"[link] (/uri)\\n\")\n    stdout = result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    print(stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert stdout.count(\"<a \") == 0\n\n\n# --- Inline form: destination and title grammar ---\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_renders_exact_element() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](/u)\") == '<a href=\"/u\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_destination_is_optional() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a]()\") == '<a href=\"\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_title_in_single_quotes() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](/u 'T')\") == '<a href=\"/u\" title=\"T\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_title_in_parentheses() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](/u (T))\") == '<a href=\"/u\" title=\"T\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_title_escaped_quote_is_unescaped_then_escaped() -> None:\n    assert parse('[a](/u \"say \\\\\"hi\\\\\"\")') == '<a href=\"/u\" title=\"say &quot;hi&quot;\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_empty_title_is_omitted() -> None:\n    assert parse('[a](/u \"\")') == '<a href=\"/u\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_angle_destination_allows_spaces() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](<my uri>)\") == '<a href=\"my%20uri\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_angle_destination_rejects_inner_angle() -> None:\n    # The `<c>` after the first `<` is a raw HTML tag, so it passes through unescaped.\n    assert parse(\"[a](<b<c>)\") == \"[a](&lt;b<c>)\"\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_balanced_parentheses_in_destination() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](foo(and(bar)))\") == '<a href=\"foo(and(bar))\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_escaped_parentheses_in_destination() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](\\\\(x\\\\))\") == '<a href=\"(x)\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_unbalanced_parenthesis_is_no_link() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](foo(bar)\") == \"[a](foo(bar)\"\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_space_in_bare_destination_is_no_link() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](my uri)\") == \"[a](my uri)\"\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_destination_is_percent_encoded() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](/ü)\") == '<a href=\"/%C3%BC\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_destination_keeps_existing_percent_escape() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](/a%20b)\") == '<a href=\"/a%20b\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_destination_entity_is_decoded_then_escaped() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](&amp;x)\") == '<a href=\"&amp;x\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_whitespace_and_one_line_ending_around_parts() -> None:\n    assert parse('[a](  /u \\n \"t\"  )') == '<a href=\"/u\" title=\"t\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_title_needs_whitespace_before_it() -> None:\n    # Without whitespace the quotes belong to the bare destination, which percent-encodes them.\n    assert parse('[a](/u\"t\")') == '<a href=\"/u%22t%22\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_title_quoted_destination_is_destination() -> None:\n    assert parse('[a](\"b\")') == '<a href=\"%22b%22\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_text_with_balanced_brackets() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a [b] c](/u)\") == '<a href=\"/u\">a [b] c</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_text_with_escaped_bracket() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a\\\\]b](/u)\") == '<a href=\"/u\">a]b</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_code_span_binds_tighter_than_bracket() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a `]`](/u)\") == '<a href=\"/u\">a <code>]</code></a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_text_holds_emphasis() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[*a*](/u)\") == '<a href=\"/u\"><em>a</em></a>'\n\n\ndef test_emphasis_can_wrap_a_link() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"*[a](/u)*\") == '<em><a href=\"/u\">a</a></em>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_ampersand_in_text_is_escaped() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a & b](/u)\") == '<a href=\"/u\">a &amp; b</a>'\n\n\n# --- Reference forms ---\n\n\ndef test_full_reference_uses_its_own_label() -> None:\n    references = references_with((\"bar\", \"/url\", None))\n    assert parse(\"[foo][bar]\", references) == '<a href=\"/url\">foo</a>'\n\n\ndef test_full_reference_with_undefined_label_is_literal() -> None:\n    references = references_with((\"foo\", \"/url\", None))\n    assert parse(\"[foo][bar]\", references) == \"[foo][bar]\"\n\n\ndef test_shortcut_before_undefined_full_label_is_not_a_link() -> None:\n    references = references_with((\"foo\", \"/url\", None))\n    assert parse(\"[foo][bar][baz]\", references) == \"[foo][bar][baz]\"\n\n\ndef test_full_reference_then_defined_label_links_the_second_pair() -> None:\n    references = references_with((\"baz\", \"/url\", None))\n    assert parse(\"[foo][bar][baz]\", references) == '[foo]<a href=\"/url\">bar</a>'\n\n\ndef test_collapsed_reference_resolves_text_as_label() -> None:\n    references = references_with((\"foo\", \"/url\", None))\n    assert parse(\"[foo][]\", references) == '<a href=\"/url\">foo</a>'\n\n\ndef test_collapsed_reference_with_undefined_label_is_literal() -> None:\n    references = references_with((\"bar\", \"/url\", None))\n    assert parse(\"[foo][]\", references) == \"[foo][]\"\n\n\ndef test_shortcut_reference_resolves_text_as_label() -> None:\n    references = references_with((\"foo\", \"/url\", None))\n    assert parse(\"[foo]\", references) == '<a href=\"/url\">foo</a>'\n\n\ndef test_shortcut_reference_with_undefined_label_is_literal() -> None:\n    references = references_with((\"foo\", \"/url\", None))\n    assert parse(\"[bar]\", references) == \"[bar]\"\n\n\ndef test_shortcut_reference_followed_by_parenthesis_that_is_no_link() -> None:\n The remaining tests compare the returned HTML string, or the executable's stdout, with its\nexact expected value. Reference maps are built per test, so no state is shared between tests.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom mdparser import inlines\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap\n\n\ndef run_executable(project_root: Path, data: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=data.encode(\"utf-8\"),\n        capture_output=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef references_with(*definitions: tuple[str, str, str | None]) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"A fresh reference map holding each (label, destination, title) definition.\"\"\"\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    for label, destination, title in definitions:\n        references.add(label, destination, title)\n    return references\n\n\ndef parse(source: str, references: ReferenceMap | None = None) -> str:\n    return inlines.parse_inline(source, references)\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Images.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_images_corpus_sections(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC images-corpus-sections: the Emphasis and strong emphasis, Links and Images sections pass.\"\"\"\n    result = subprocess.run(\n        [\n            sys.executable,\n            \"sources/spec_tests.py\",\n            \"--program\",\n            str(project_root / \"commonmark\"),\n            \"--spec\",\n            \"sources/spec.txt\",\n            \"--pattern\",\n            \"^Emphasis and strong emphasis$|^Links$|^Images$\",\n        ],\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n    print(result.stdout)\n    print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n\n\ndef test_images_inline_image(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC images-inline-image: an inline image renders one img element carrying the supplied src, alt and title.\"\"\"\n    alt = \"my alt\"\n    src = \"/path/pic.jpg\"\n    title = \"a title\"\n    source = \"![\" + alt + \"](\" + src + ' \"' + title + '\")\\n'\n    result = subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<img \") == 1\n    assert ('src=\"' + src + '\"') in result.stdout\n    assert ('alt=\"' + alt + '\"') in result.stdout\n    assert ('title=\"' + title + '\"') in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_images_alt_is_plain_text(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC images-alt-is-plain-text: emphasis inside an image description does not appear as markup in alt.\"\"\"\n    result = subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=\"![foo *bar*](/u)\\n\",\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<img \") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_images_reference_forms(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC images-reference-forms: full, collapsed and shortcut image references each resolve against a definition.\"\"\"\n    definition = \"\\n\\n[foo]: /url\\n\"\n    for use in (\"![text][foo]\", \"![foo][]\", \"![foo]\"):\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n            input=use + definition,\n            capture_output=True,\n            text=True,\n            cwd=project_root,\n            check=False,\n        )\n        print(result.stdout)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<img \") == 1\n\n\ndef test_images_inside_link(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC images-inside-link: an image inside a link produces one a element containing one img element.\"\"\"\n    result = subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=\"[![moon](moon.jpg)](/uri)\\n\",\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<a \") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<img \") == 1\n\n\n# --- Inline form: attributes ---\n\n\ndef test_inline_image_without_title_has_no_title_attribute() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"![foo](/url)\") == '<img src=\"/url\" alt=\"foo\" />'\n\n\ndef test_inline_image_with_title() -> None:\n    assert parse('![foo](/url \"title\")') == '<img src=\"/url\" alt=\"foo\" title=\"title\" />'\n\n\ndef test_inline_image_with_empty_description_has_empty_alt() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"![](/url)\") == '<img src=\"/url\" alt=\"\" />'\n\n\ndef test_image_title_is_escaped() -> None:\n    assert parse('![a](/u \"x&y\")') == '<img src=\"/u\" alt=\"a\" title=\"x&amp;y\" />'\n\n\ndef test_image_src_is_percent_encoded() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"![a](</a b>)\") == '<img src=\"/a%20b\" alt=\"a\" />'\n\n\ndef test_image_src_is_percent_encoded_for_non_ascii() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"![a](/é)\") == '<img src=\"/%C3%A9\" alt=\"a\" />'\n\n\n# --- Alt text is the plain text of the description ---\n\n\ndef test_alt_drops_strong_emphasis_markup() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"![foo **bar**](/u)\") == '<img src=\"/u\" alt=\"foo bar\" />'\n\n\ndef test_alt_keeps_code_span_content() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"![foo `bar`](/u)\") == '<img src=\"/u\" alt=\"foo bar\" />'\n\n\ndef test_alt_keeps_link_text_and_drops_the_link() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"![foo [bar](/url)](/url2)\") == '<img src=\"/url2\" alt=\"foo bar\" />'\n\n\ndef test_alt_takes_the_alt_of_a_nested_image() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"![foo ![bar](/url)](/url2)\") == '<img src=\"/url2\" alt=\"foo bar\" />'\n\n\ndef test_alt_keeps_autolink_text() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"![<http://x.y>](/u)\") == '<img src=\"/u\" alt=\"http://x.y\" />'\n\n\ndef test_alt_is_escaped_text() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"![a<b&c](/u)\") == '<img src=\"/u\" alt=\"a&lt;b&amp;c\" />'\n\n\ndef test_alt_keeps_an_escaped_punctuation_character_as_text() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"![a\\\\*b](/u)\") == '<img src=\"/u\" alt=\"a*b\" />'\n\n\ndef test_alt_decodes_a_character_reference() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"![&copy;](/u)\") == '<img src=\"/u\" alt=\"©\" />'\n\n\n# --- Reference forms ---\n\n\ndef test_full_reference_image_uses_its_text_as_alt() -> None:\n    references = references_with((\"foo\", \"/url\", None))\n    assert parse(\"![text][foo]\", references) == '<img src=\"/url\" alt=\"text\" />'\n\n\ndef test_collapsed_reference_image_uses_its_label_as_alt() -> None:\n    references = references_with((\"foo\", \"/url\", None))\n    assert parse(\"![foo][]\", references) == '<img src=\"/url\" alt=\"foo\" />'\n\n\ndef test_shortcut_reference_image_uses_its_label_as_alt() -> None:\n    references = references_with((\"foo\", \"/url\", None))\n    assert parse(\"![foo]\", references) == '<img src=\"/url\" alt=\"foo\" />'\n\n\ndef test_reference_image_carries_the_definition_title() -> None:\n    references = references_with((\"foo\", \"/url\", \"t\"))\n    assert parse(\"![foo]\", references) == '<img src=\"/url\" alt=\"foo\" title=\"t\" />'\n\n\ndef test_unresolved_shortcut_image_is_literal_text() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"![foo]\") == \"![foo]\"\n\n\ndef test_unresolved_full_reference_fails_the_whole_image() -> None:\n    references = references_with((\"foo\", \"/url\", None))\n    assert parse(\"![text][bar]\", references) == \"![text][bar]\"\n\n\n# --- Interaction with the other constructs ---\n\n\ndef test_image_inside_link_renders_one_anchor_around_one_image() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[![moon](moon.jpg)](/uri)\") == (\n        '<a href=\"/uri\"><img src=\"moon.jpg\" alt=\"moon\" /></a>'\n    )\n\n\ndef test_image_in_running_text_keeps_surrounding_text() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"My ![foo](/path) here\") == 'My <img src=\"/path\" alt=\"foo\" /> here'\n\n\ndef test_escaped_bang_leaves_a_link_after_it() -> None:\n    references = references_with((\"foo\", \"/url\", None))\n    assert parse(\"\\\\![foo]\", references) == '!<a href=\"/url\">foo</a>'\n\n\ndef test_escaped_opening_bracket_after_bang_is_literal() -> None:\n    references = references_with((\"foo\", \"/url\", None))\n    assert parse(\"!\\\\[foo]\", references) == \"![foo]\"\n\n\n# --- Executable ---\n\n\ndef test_executable_renders_an_image_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"![foo](/url)\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout == b'<p><img src=\"/url\" alt=\"foo\" /></p>\\n'\n\n\ndef test_executable_resolves_an_image_reference_definition(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"![foo]\\n\\n[foo]: /url\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01S3ZHDAWNG3Cq9EU4sMBSWK","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/tests/test_links.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1426ab3b-27b1-4ec8-bce6-bdc563b1d55e","uuid":"ef1c39e9-ed94-40cb-a78f-212027103b8a","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:45:26.316Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/tests/test_links.py","oldString":"    assert parse(\"[a ![b](/i) c](/u)\") == '<a href=\"/u\">a ![b](/i) c</a>'","newString":"    assert parse(\"[a ![b](/i) c](/u)\") == '<a href=\"/u\">a <img src=\"/i\" alt=\"b\" /> c</a>'","originalFile":"\"\"\"Link tests: the look-for-link-or-image procedure, inline and reference forms, and their grammar.\n\nThe declared acceptance checks are transcribed from FEATURE-Links.md with their assertions kept as\nwritten. The remaining tests compare the returned HTML string, or the executable's stdout, with its\nexact expected value. Reference maps are built per test, so no state is shared between tests.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom mdparser import inlines\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap\n\n\ndef run_executable(project_root: Path, data: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=data.encode(\"utf-8\"),\n        capture_output=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef references_with(*definitions: tuple[str, str, str | None]) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"A fresh reference map holding each (label, destination, title) definition.\"\"\"\n    references = ReferenceMap()\n    for label, destination, title in definitions:\n        references.add(label, destination, title)\n    return references\n\n\ndef parse(source: str, references: ReferenceMap | None = None) -> str:\n    return inlines.parse_inline(source, references)\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Links.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_links_inline_destination_and_title(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC links-inline-destination-and-title: an inline link renders one a element with its parts.\"\"\"\n    text = \"label\"\n    dest = \"/uri\"\n    title = \"the title\"\n    source = \"[\" + text + \"](\" + dest + ' \"' + title + '\")\\n'\n    result = subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<a \") == 1\n    assert ('href=\"' + dest + '\"') in result.stdout\n    assert ('title=\"' + title + '\"') in result.stdout\n    assert (\">\" + text + \"</a>\") in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_links_reference_forms(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC links-reference-forms: full, collapsed and shortcut references each render one a element.\"\"\"\n    definition = \"\\n\\n[foo]: /url\\n\"\n    for use in (\"[text][foo]\", \"[foo][]\", \"[foo]\"):\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n            input=(use + definition).encode(\"utf-8\"),\n            capture_output=True,\n            cwd=project_root,\n            check=False,\n        )\n        print(result.stdout)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\").count(\"<a \") == 1\n\n\ndef test_links_reference_case_insensitive(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC links-reference-case-insensitive: label matching ignores case.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"[FOO]\\n\\n[foo]: /url\\n\")\n    stdout = result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    print(stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert stdout.count(\"<a \") == 1\n\n\ndef test_links_undefined_reference_literal(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC links-undefined-reference-literal: a shortcut reference with no definition stays literal.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"[nothing defined]\\n\")\n    stdout = result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    print(stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert stdout.count(\"<a \") == 0\n\n\ndef test_links_no_nested_links(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC links-no-nested-links: a link inside link text wins and the outer brackets stay literal.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"[foo [bar](/uri)](/uri)\\n\")\n    stdout = result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    print(stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert stdout.count(\"<a \") == 1\n\n\ndef test_links_space_before_parenthesis(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"AC links-space-before-parenthesis: whitespace between link text and the parenthesis is no link.\"\"\"\n    result = run_executable(project_root, \"[link] (/uri)\\n\")\n    stdout = result.stdout.decode(\"utf-8\")\n    print(stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert stdout.count(\"<a \") == 0\n\n\n# --- Inline form: destination and title grammar ---\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_renders_exact_element() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](/u)\") == '<a href=\"/u\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_destination_is_optional() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a]()\") == '<a href=\"\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_title_in_single_quotes() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](/u 'T')\") == '<a href=\"/u\" title=\"T\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_title_in_parentheses() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](/u (T))\") == '<a href=\"/u\" title=\"T\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_title_escaped_quote_is_unescaped_then_escaped() -> None:\n    assert parse('[a](/u \"say \\\\\"hi\\\\\"\")') == '<a href=\"/u\" title=\"say &quot;hi&quot;\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_empty_title_is_omitted() -> None:\n    assert parse('[a](/u \"\")') == '<a href=\"/u\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_angle_destination_allows_spaces() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](<my uri>)\") == '<a href=\"my%20uri\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_angle_destination_rejects_inner_angle() -> None:\n    # The `<c>` after the first `<` is a raw HTML tag, so it passes through unescaped.\n    assert parse(\"[a](<b<c>)\") == \"[a](&lt;b<c>)\"\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_balanced_parentheses_in_destination() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](foo(and(bar)))\") == '<a href=\"foo(and(bar))\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_escaped_parentheses_in_destination() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](\\\\(x\\\\))\") == '<a href=\"(x)\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_unbalanced_parenthesis_is_no_link() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](foo(bar)\") == \"[a](foo(bar)\"\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_space_in_bare_destination_is_no_link() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](my uri)\") == \"[a](my uri)\"\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_destination_is_percent_encoded() -> None:\n    assert parse(\"[a](/ü)\") == '<a href=\"/%C3%BC\">a</a>'\n\n\ndef test_inline_link_destination_keeps_existing_percent_escape() -> The alt is the plain text of the description: emphasis, links and nested images contribute their text, code spans contribute their content, and the result is escaped.\n\nTo get plain text, `Html` nodes now carry a `text` field alongside their rendered HTML.
